finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a malicious file path that includes shell metacharacters or control operators.
finding.assumptions: The filePath is derived from untrusted input and the environment where this code runs allows shell metacharacters to be interpreted.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that std::ifstream::open(filePath.c_str()) does not invoke a shell or interpret metacharacters; it simply opens a file by path. No command execution occurs, so OS command injection is impossible.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: An attacker can provide a malicious regex pattern that includes shell metacharacters or control operators.
finding.assumptions: The query is derived from untrusted input and the environment where this code runs allows shell metacharacters to be interpreted.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink is the std::regex constructor at line 27. The std::regex constructor compiles a regular expression pattern; it does not invoke a shell or execute system commands. Therefore, even if the query string contains shell metacharacters, they are treated as literal regex characters and cannot influence command execution. No other checks or sanitisation are required for this operation, and the code does not perform any command execution. Hence, the claim of OS Command Injection is unfounded.

The string constructed at line 36 is only stored in a struct and never passed to a command‑execution API. Therefore, even if filePath contains shell metacharacters, they are not interpreted by a shell. The reported sink is not a command execution sink, so OS Command Injection does not occur here.
